major_concerns: Validator-oracle specification is underspecified (which static checks / Batfish rules exactly?).
Dataset representativeness: public examples may not match operational distributions—threat to external validity.
Single-LLM single-version dependence not explicit; results may not generalize across models/versions.
Handling of ambiguous validator outcomes (human adjudication) is not fully defined and may breach autonomy/reproducibility constraints.
Recovery from API rate limits or transient failures and retry-policy effects on paired design need clarity.
required_design_repairs: Specify exact validator toolchain (versions, rule-set files) and provide test oracle examples; publish validator code/config.
Define task sourcing and sampling procedure with provenance, training/held-out split, and sanitization steps.
Fix model details: explicit provider, model identifier(s), exact prompt templates, temperature schedule, seeds, and number of calls per sample; snapshot and publish raw outputs.

Replace or tightly predefine any human adjudication: either use deterministic tie-breaker rules or pre-register a blinded automated adjudicator; if human review unavoidable, preregister selection/rubric and log every decision.
Pre-register retry policy, rate-limit handling, failure classification, and how truncated runs are analyzed; include hash-signed execution logs for reproducibility.

major_concerns: Simulator fidelity and ecological validity are primary threats—synthetic faults may not map to real device semantics.
Auditability score is subjective as stated; inter-rater reliability and rubric are not defined.
Ensuring parity of oracle/tool access between orchestration patterns must be explicit to avoid confounding.
Agentic pipeline safety controls (iteration caps, loop detection) are only loosely specified; risk of runaway agent loops.
Randomization and sample size justification for 240 tasks needs formal power analysis.
required_design_repairs: Specify simulator/emulation platform (versions), fault-injection semantics, and provide validation that simulator reproduces key vendor behaviors.
Publish a detailed auditability scoring rubric, run an inter-rater calibration on a held pilot set, and report kappa/ICC before main analysis.
Define strict oracle/tool access parity and instrument access logs to show equivalence; pre-register permitted tool queries for the agent.
Specify agent safeguards: explicit iteration/step caps, loop detection heuristics, and abort conditions; log all agent decisions.
Provide power/sample-size calculation for harmful-change rate comparison and preregister stratification by task complexity; publish randomization seed and assignment manifest.

major_concerns: Planned human-reviewed tie-breaker for ambiguous validator outcomes conflicts with the autonomy/reproducibility mandate unless tightly specified.
'Validator budget' levels are described qualitatively; exact validator computation/timeout/resource definitions are needed.
Censoring/truncation risk when model-call budget exhausted must be handled statistically.
Task provenance (postmortem vs synthetic) may bias results; mixing sources requires stratification.
Potential overfitting of policy recommendations to the synthetic/curated task set threatens external validity.
required_design_repairs: Remove open-ended human adjudication or replace with pre-registered deterministic adjudication heuristics; if human review used, define reviewer pool, rubric, blinding, and log all decisions.
Precisely define validator-budget levels (static checks list, topology checks algorithm, simulator dry-run spec) with resource/time caps and versioned implementations.
Pre-register censoring-handling rules and plan (e.g., treat exhausted-budget runs as censored and apply survival/competing-risk analysis).
Document task sourcing with provenance tags, stratify analyses by source (postmortem vs synthetic), and preregister exclusion rules.
Add external-validation holdout or small production-like sample if possible, and explicitly bound recommendations to dataset characteristics.

major_concerns: Automated trace-scoring may be brittle and favor particular surface forms; heuristics need robust specification and validation.
Benchmark task and oracle design choices can privilege certain models—task curation and diversity procedures must be transparent.
Publishing configuration examples and traces risks exposing sensitive practices; sanitization policy required.
Model-version drift for hosted models threatens reproducibility if baseline outputs are not snapshot/signed.
Scoring calibration (thresholds for 'verifiability') is underspecified.
required_design_repairs: Define and publish the trace-scoring algorithm with test cases, include human spot-checks for rubric calibration, and report scoring reliability metrics.
Provide explicit task-sourcing policy to ensure vendor/mode diversity; publish provenance and selection criteria.
Apply and describe sanitization procedures for all artifacts and document legal/ethical review of released content.
Snapshot and publish baseline model outputs, exact prompts, and model-version identifiers; include Docker/VM images for evaluation code where possible.
Pre-register verifiability thresholds and run sensitivity analyses showing how conclusions change with threshold variation.
